text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on July 20 in history.
1304 - The poet Petrarch born Francesco Petrarca. One of the greatest lyric poets and the earliest of the Italian Renaissance, he is bext known for his collection of sonnets "To Laura".
1402 - Tamerlane, leading a massive force of Tartars, defeated and captured the Sultan of the Ottoman Empire at the Battle of Angora (now Ankara).
1654 - Portugal was placed under English control following the signing of the Anglo-Portuguese treaty.
1785 - Mahmud II, Sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1808-39, born.
1847 - Max Liebermann, German post-impressionist painter and etcher, born.
1866 - In the Seven Weeks' War the Austrians partially destroyed the Italian fleet at Lissa Island, killing over 1,100.
1890 - George II, King of Greece, born. From 1922 until his death in 1947, he alternated between periods of exile and rule.
1893 - Alexander, King of Greece from 1917-20, born; he is believed to be the only monarch to have died after being bitten by a monkey.
1903 - Pope Leo XIII (Gioacchino Vincenzo Pecci) died; he had been Pope since 1878.
1913 - Turkey re-entered the Balkan conflict and captured Adrianople from Bulgaria.
1917 - The Pact of Corfu was agreed under which Serbs, Croats and Slovenes agreed to form a union called Yugoslavia.
1919 - Sir Edmund Hillary, conqueror of Mount Everest in 1953, born in New Zealand.
1924 - Elias Sarkis, Lebanese statesman and president from 1976-82, born.
1925 - Jacques Delors, French statesman and president of the European Commission from 1985-94, born.
1927 - Ferdinand I of Romania died and was succeeded by his grandson, Prince Michael.
1937 - Guglielmo Marconi, Italian physicist and pioneer of wireless telegraphy, died.
1938 - Natalie Wood, U.S. film actress, born as Natasha Gurdin; best known originally for "Miracle on 34th Street" as a child star and later for "Rebel without a Cause" and "West Side Story".
1944 - Claus Schenk Graf von Stauffenberg made an unsuccessful attempt to assassinate Adolf Hitler by planting a bomb under his table in the "Wolf's Lair" headquarters.
1951 - King Abdullah of Jordan was assassinated when entering a mosque in Jerusalem; he had been king from 1946.
1954 - Armistice for Indo-China was signed, under which Vietnam was separated into North and South.
1958 - King Hussein of Jordan broke off diplomatic relations with the United Arab Republic after complaining of its threats and aggression.
1969 - U.S. astronaut Neil Armstrong stepped from the lunar module Eagle to become the first man to walk on the moon. He said "That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind".
1973 - A Japan Air Lines Boeing 747 was hijacked over the Netherlands. Four days later via a stop at Dubai it was blown up at Benghazi.
1974 - Turkish armed forces invaded the northern part of Cyprus, shelling Kyrenia and moving inland towards Nicosia.
1976 - Viking 1, the unmanned U.S. spacecraft, ended its 11-month journey with a touchdown on Mars.
1982 - In central London 10 soldiers were killed in IRA bomb explosions in Hyde Park and Regents Park.
1988 - South Africa, Cuba and Angola reached agreement in principle on a plan to end the war in Angola and grant independence to Namibia.
1989 - Burmese opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi was placed under house arrest for her outspoken attacks on the country's military rulers.
1992 - Vaclav Havel stepped down as President of Czechoslovakia as the country moved further toward a permanent split.
1994 - Foreign Minister Shimon Peres became the highest-ranking Israeli official to set foot in Jordan.
1996 - Hutu rebels attacked Bungendana refugee camp in Burundi, killing at least 300.
